input:
#NEXUS

begin trees;
translate

3 t1,
4 't2 the name'
,1 'isn''that [a] strange name?',
2 'one should be punished, for (that)!'
,
9 t5,
7 t6  ,
8 t7,
5
t8, 6 t9;

tree tree1 = [&R] [&W3.5] (1,(2,3),(4,(5,6,(7,(8,9)))));
end;
note: TRANSLATE with ids out of order, commas on their own lines and leading commas, quoted labels with doubled apostrophe, brackets, comma and parentheses; tree has [&R] and [&W3.5]; the library only checks it parses and later prints the quoted names.
Three trees all named tree1 (duplicate names, last has branch lengths and numeric internal labels); library keeps all three in order (test indexes n.trees[2]); first tree is the answer for a viewer.
Underscore versus quoted-space labels through TRANSLATE; first of two trees must be used. Derived from the standard, not asserted by the library.
Plain comments (nested, and one containing [& inside) between blocks must be stripped; library parses the whole file and expects no error.

Non-tree DATA block with interleaved rows where one name is quoted-with-space in block 1 and underscored in block 2; library expects them treated as the same taxon (NexusTest1). The tree must be unaffected (DendroPy reads it; Biopython keeps quotes on stored names after TRANSLATE).
Unknown block with free text and semicolons before TREES; library reads it into unknown_blocks and ignores it.

TreeBASE layout: [! header comment with colons and parens, TAXA with TAXLABELS, TITLE and LINK TAXA in TREES, tree name 'Fig._1', support labels on internal nodes; shrunk from the 658-taxon file, library only asserts it reads; DendroPy agrees on the labels.

source: Bio/Nexus/Nexus.py _tree (comment: 'a star can be used to make it the default tree'); no test
note: TREE * name marks the default tree; library skips the star. Not asserted by its tests.
Obsolete UTREE command, used by ClustalX, treated like TREE with rooted=False; DendroPy 5.1.3 finds no tree (IndexError) so readers disagree.
Rooting flag comments in front of the tree string; library sets rooted from them and requires '&' as first char (any other [x..] there raises NexusError).

Standard allows [&W 1/2] as a rational; Biopython does float('1/2') and is expected to fail (see _tree), so readers that mirror it will raise; a viewer should ignore the weight; DendroPy reads the tree fine. Library has no test for this.
Numeric tip names without TRANSLATE, [&..] comments after a leaf name, after an internal node and after the root with no closing branch length; library expects these comments stored per node.

TreeAnnotator-style [&key={a,b}] comments whose commas, braces and percent signs must not split children; here a unary chain of internal nodes also appears; library expects the leaf names 9 and 5 and the branch lengths.
Text labels on internal nodes and root (names, not support); library expects node taxa Taxaceae, TT1 on the internals; tips are the three leaves.
Numeric internal labels (support values) and a numeric root label; library reads 25 and 90 as branch length of those nodes, not as taxa, and has_support() is False.

Quoted tip name with a space directly in the Newick (no TRANSLATE) mixed with plain ones; labels per the standard (quotes removed); Biopython and DendroPy both read it, but Biopython keeps the quotes in the stored name; its own tests only use quoted names through TRANSLATE.

source: Bio/Nexus/Trees.py (comment: ( ) and : not allowed in taxon names) and test_TreeTest1
note: Standard NEXUS allows these in quoted labels; Biopython's Newick parser counts raw parentheses and finds colons, so it splits it into mangled labels while DendroPy returns the labels correctly; its own tests only reach such names via TRANSLATE.

source: Bio/Nexus/Nexus.py _tree ('Unable to substitute %s using translate data.')
note: Tip id 3 has no TRANSLATE entry; Biopython raises NexusError; the NEXUS standard says the label is then the literal token, so tip labels left null (reader disagreement: DendroPy returns a, b and the literal 3).
TRANSLATE whose labels are themselves numbers; substitution is one pass over tokens, so the tree (1,(2,3)) becomes (3,(1,2)).
Tree-only file with no TAXA block; translate across several lines, last entry without trailing comma.
The exact layout Bio.Phylo.NexusIO.write emits (mixed-case keywords, no spaces around '=' in 'tree tree1=(...)', no translate).
Upper/mixed-case keywords and '=' glued to the name.
Tree string spread over lines, including a line break before the terminating semicolon; library joins lines (note: a quoted label spanning lines would lose its newline).
Windows line endings, including inside TRANSLATE; library normalises them.

input: #NEXUSbegin trees;tree t = ((a,b),c);end;
note: Classic Mac line endings; library converts a bare CR to a newline.
SETS block with charset, taxset and taxpartition between DATA and TREES must not disturb tree reading.

source: Bio/Nexus/Nexus.py read() (comment: '#NEXUS token - in merged treefiles, this might appear multiple times')
note: Concatenated tree files each starting with #NEXUS; library drops the repeated token and reads both trees in order; first tree is a,b,c.

Deliberately unbalanced parentheses (one extra open): library's Tree._parse raises TreeError 'Parentheses do not match'; no library test asserts the failure on a file, so tip labels null; DendroPy also rejects it, and wellFormed=false is a judgement, not a library assertion.
Stray ']' outside a comment: library raises NexusError; not exercised by its tests, so wellFormed is a judgement from the code, not an assertion; DendroPy silently accepts it (readers disagree).
oursWhy: a stray ] is part of a name; DendroPy accepts it too

note: Unterminated comment swallows the rest of the file; library raises NexusError (code, not asserted by a test), and DendroPy fails too (IndexError).
